original_value: A Virtual Learning Environment (VLE) is an accumulation of incorporated soft-ware components, empowering the administration of web-based learning (online learning, e-learning). The quality of VLE is indispensable for the accomplishment of e-learning goals and responsible to engage students during web based learning. The attributes of existing VLES does not completely meet with the requirements of today’s e-learning. Consequently, decreases students’ interest, participation and engagement with web-based e-learning. In contrast, the learners’ engagement and participation are higher in social networking sites (SNS). For this reason, many researchers believe that the inclusion of features, similar to SNSs, in VLE may in-crease its effectivity. The goal of this research article is to investigate existing e-learning platform and make a room for SNSs and online tools for e-learning. The paper proposes an integrated model to enhance existing e-learning environment by incorporating the strength of SNSs and other potential tools with VLEs. This re-search article will provide a good direction and new thoughts for the researchers of technology supported learning-domain.

result.paraphrase: A Virtual Learning Environment (VLE) is a collection of integrated software components that supports the management of web-based learning, also known as online learning or e-learning. VLE quality is essential to achieving e-learning goals and to keeping students engaged in web-based learning. However, current VLEs do not fully satisfy today’s e-learning requirements, which reduces students’ interest, participation, and engagement. By contrast, learner engagement and participation are higher on social networking sites (SNS). For this reason, many researchers argue that adding SNS-like features to VLEs could improve their effectiveness. This research article aims to examine existing e-learning platforms and create space for SNSs and online tools in e-learning. It proposes an integrated model to improve the current e-learning environment by combining the strengths of SNSs and other potential tools with VLEs. The article offers useful guidance and fresh ideas for researchers in the field of technology-supported learning.
